newsitem.title: USA: Disruptive air passengers charged in Los Angeles.
newsitem.headline: Disruptive air passengers charged in Los Angeles.

text.p: Two passengers who became unruly after being denied a first-class upgrade and tried to enter an airliner's cockpit during a flight were charged Tuesday with interfering with a flight crew.

Thomas Kasper, 36, and Susan Callihan, 28, both of southern California, were arrested at Los Angeles International Airport Monday evening after the incident, in which hot coffee was thrown on two flight attendants.
U.S. Attorney Nora Manella said the two appeared in court before U.S. District Judge Andrew Wistrich, who ordered them held in lieu of $50,000 bond on the federal charge.
In a statement, Manella said the pair became disruptive on Continental Airlines Flight 1837 after being denied a request for an upgrade to the first-class section of the plane.
Kasper went to the galley and grabbed two coffee pots, which he wielded as weapons, according to an affidavit by Kevin Lammons, a Federal Bureau of Investigation agent.
Kasper poured hot coffee on two attendants, causing second-degree burns on the hand of one of the crew members.
An airport police spokesman said Monday night the woman "was banging on the cockpit door and yelling she had a gun."

All of the passengers on the Houston to Los Angeles flight were evacuated. The aircraft was then towed to a remote area of the airport and searched by the bomb squad after police received a report of a suspicious looking package. Police said no bomb was found.
